original_title: Marvel’s Spider-Man 2’s Finishing Moves Inspired Tom Holland for Spider-Man: Brand New Day
summary_en: Tom Holland revealed that the finishing moves from Insomniac's acclaimed Marvel's Spider-Man games directly influenced his portrayal of the web-slinger in the upcoming film, Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The inspiration even extended to the film's design and stunt teams.
ai_analysis: This cross-pollination between video games and blockbuster cinema highlights the growing cultural impact of interactive entertainment and the deep fandom that exists even among Hollywood's creative talent.

en.title: Tom Holland Borrowed Spider-Man: Insomniac's Moves for 'Brand New Day'
en.summary: Tom Holland revealed that the finishing moves from Insomniac's acclaimed Marvel's Spider-Man games directly influenced his portrayal of the web-slinger in the upcoming film, Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The inspiration even extended to the film's design and stunt teams.
en.body:
The upcoming theatrical release of **Marvel's Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is already generating significant buzz, and star **Tom Holland** has offered a fascinating glimpse into his preparation. In a recent interview, Holland shared that he found inspiration for his on-screen heroics not from comic books or previous films, but from the digital prowess of Insomniac Games' **Marvel's Spider-Man** series. He admitted to recently revisiting the games, finding himself so engrossed that he couldn't sleep.

"A lot of the finishing moves. I was actually playing the game last night. I couldn’t sleep last night; I was so excited about today. I was trying to figure out what I was gonna do, and I was like, ‘I’ll just throw the game on and have some fun.’ For me, a lot of those finishing moves, a lot of our stuff was influenced by that stuff," Holland told IGN. This connection between the virtual and the cinematic extends beyond the lead actor, with **Director Destin Daniel Cretton** also confirming the significant influence of Insomniac's work on his crew.


## Digital Inspirations for Real-World Action

A substantial portion of the film's creative team, particularly those in design and stunt coordination, were avid players of Insomniac's **Marvel's Spider-Man** and **Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales**. These passionate gamers brought their enthusiasm directly into the filmmaking process, using the games as a visual and kinetic reference. The director elaborated on how these team members would meticulously capture screenshots of particularly impressive in-game maneuvers.

"A lot of the action designers and stunt people we had were huge gamers," Cretton explained. "They were able to experience things in those games that made them excited, and they would just screengrab the moves they really liked and bring them into the writers’ room and show it to me. And then we’d be like, ‘Yeah, that’s sick. Let’s try to figure out how to do that for real.’" This collaborative approach underscores how deeply integrated gaming has become within broader entertainment production, influencing everything from character animation to practical stunt work.


## A Symbiotic Relationship Between Media

This revelation is a testament to the artistry and innovation present in Insomniac's **Spider-Man** titles. The studio has consistently delivered games that not only capture the spirit of the character but also push the boundaries of superhero action in interactive media. For **Tom Holland**, who has embodied Spider-Man in the Marvel Cinematic Universe since his debut in 2016's **Captain America: Civil War**, finding fresh ways to portray the iconic hero is an ongoing challenge. The intricate, dynamic, and often brutal finishing moves found in the games likely provided a rich wellspring of inspiration for choreographing new sequences that feel both familiar and exhilarating.


## What's Next

**Spider-Man: Brand New Day** is set to swing into theaters soon, continuing **Tom Holland**'s journey as the friendly neighborhood hero. Fans will undoubtedly be watching closely to see which specific moves and sequences bear the unmistakable mark of Insomniac's beloved video game adaptations.

In an interview with IGN , he spoke about recently playing them again, as well as how he based some of his own moves in the film on the finishing moves from the Insomniac games. “A lot of the finishing moves. I was actually playing the game last night. I couldn’t sleep last night; I was so excited about today. I was trying to figure out what I was gonna do, and I was like, ‘I’ll just throw the game on and have some fun.’ For me, a lot of those finishing moves, a lot of our stuff was influenced by that stuff.” Director Destin Daniel Cretton also revealed that plenty of people among the design and stunt crew were also fans of Insomniac’s Marvel’s Spider-Man series. Some even went as far as to bring in screenshots from the games to the writers’ room. “A lot of the action designers and stunt people we had were huge gamers,” he said. “They were able to experience things in those games that made them excited, and they would just screengrab the moves they really liked and bring them into the writers’ room and show it to me. And then we’d be like, ‘Yeah, that’s sick. Let’s try to figure out how to do that for real.’” Holland has played the role of Spider-Man in the MCU since he first made his debut as the character in 2016’s Captain America: Civil War . The character would go on to get his own standalone movies beginning with 2017’s Spider-Man: Homecoming . The character has also shown up in other MCU movies, including crossovers like Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame . Spider-Man: Brand New Day is going to be the fourth mainline MCU Spider-Man film, with its story taking place around four years after the events of 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home . The core narrative will revolve around Peter Parker uncovering a mystery that hints at larger threats than he has faced in the past, as well as his body undergoing strange new mutations, giving him abilities that he may not yet be able to control. Along with Holland, the film will see many actors reprising their roles, including Zendaya as Michelle Jones-Watson, Jacob Batalon as Ned Leeds, and Michael Mando as Mac Gargan and The Scorpion. Newer cast members will include Mark Ruffalo reprising his role as Bruce Banner and The Hulk and Jon Bernthal returning as Frank Castle and The Punisher. Celebrating the release of the movie, as well as the upcoming launch of fighting game Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls , Insomniac Games recently released a free update for Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 , introducing a pair of new suits to the game. The PS5 version of the game got more things in the update, like support for Enhanced PSSR and Power Saver Mode.
